name: Prisma
description: Type-safe ORM and schema tooling for Node.js and TypeScript.
why: A common default for typed database access and migrations.

name: Drizzle ORM
description: SQL-first TypeScript ORM with a lightweight runtime.
why: Good when you want explicit SQL shape and minimal abstraction.

name: Supabase
description: Postgres backend with auth, storage, realtime, and generated APIs.
why: A fast path from schema to working auth and data APIs.

name: Neon
description: Serverless Postgres with branching and scale-to-zero.
why: Useful for preview environments and agent-created branches.

name: PlanetScale
description: Managed MySQL-compatible database with branching workflows.
why: A mature managed database option for MySQL-shaped apps.

name: PostgreSQL
description: Open-source relational database with strong correctness and extension support.
why: The safest default relational database for new production apps.

name: Redis
description: In-memory data store for caching, queues, and realtime state.
why: Common infrastructure for caching and rate limiting; check license terms.

name: Zod
description: TypeScript-first schema validation with static type inference.
why: A clean way to validate inputs at API and form boundaries.

name: OpenAPI
description: Standard specification for describing HTTP APIs.
why: Gives agents and tools a machine-readable API contract.

name: Postman
description: API client, collections, and collaboration platform.
why: Widely used for manual API verification and sharing requests.

name: Hoppscotch
description: Open-source API client that runs in the browser or self-hosted.
why: A lightweight, open alternative to hosted API clients.

name: dbt
description: SQL-based transformation framework with tests, docs, and lineage.
why: The standard way to make warehouse transformations reviewable.

name: BigQuery
why: Common production warehouse target for dbt and analytics work.

name: DuckDB
why: Excellent for local data exploration and reproducible analysis.

name: Apache Airflow
why: A standard choice for batch data pipelines.

name: n8n
description: Visual workflow automation with code nodes and self-hosting.
why: Fast way to connect APIs and agents without building a scheduler.

name: Laravel Boost
description: Laravel's MCP server and agent guidelines for application-aware coding.
why: The canonical way to give an agent Laravel-specific context and tools.

name: PacketLark
description: Local API workbench and HTTP contract engine maintained by this repository's author.
why: Useful for request replay, mock servers, and HTTP contract testing.
